subtopic: Lock-Free Data Structures and Atomic Primitives
question_text: Why does the Michael & Scott lock-free queue algorithm require a dummy head node?

options.text: To prevent cache line invalidation between head and tail pointers
To ensure the queue is never truly empty, decoupling enqueue and dequeue pointer manipulations so they do not contend on the same node pointer when size is 0
To store the queue size counter atomically
To allow backward traversal in double-ended queues

answer_explanation: With a sentinel dummy node, `head` and `tail` never point to null. Dequeue updates `head->next`, while enqueue updates `tail->next`, eliminating race conditions when transitioning between 0 and 1 items.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: With a sentinel dummy node, `head` and `tail` never point to null. Dequeue updates `head->next`, while enqueue updates `tail->next`, eliminating race conditions when transitioning between 0 and 1 items.
